subject: Mutual action plan: evidence collection, SLA gating & signature timeline
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@cardinalhealth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual action plan: evidence collection, SLA gating & signature timeline

Hi Elena —

Great talking earlier. Per our discussion, I put together a short mutual action plan (attached) that sequences the legal/procurement steps and maps acceptance gates to evidence items so procurement can lock the order form without delaying the pilot. High-level proposed cadence:

1) Week 0 (this week): Exchange draft MSA+DPA redlines. Redwood will provide initial redline (attached: redline_msadpa_v1.pdf).
2) Week 1: Cardinal review of DPA and SOC2 artefacts. If SOC2 evidence acceptable, Procurement can issue a PO stub to reserve capacity (procurement_PO_stub.pdf).
3) Week 2: Pilot activation (canary) — 2-week evaluation with acceptance criteria (latency, feature coverage, data handling checks).
4) Week 4: Post-pilot acceptance and signature of order form; formal MSA signature targeted in parallel, DPA finalized by legal sign-off.

Key gating items we need from you to avoid blowups:
- SOC2 report (latest) or cross-walk to Cardinal controls
- SSO/SAML IdP metadata and a sandbox service account for the pilot
- Confirmation whether Cardinal requires data residency contract language (if yes, scope of regions)

I attached the MAP spreadsheet with owners and dates (naomi_MAP_v1.xlsx). Can you confirm procurement's target approval window and whether the PO stub is a helpful step?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20m call to walk through owners.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior GTM Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morris <elena@cardinalhealth.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cardinalhealth.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Jun 2025 11:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: evidence collection, SLA gating & signature timeline

Naomi —

Thanks for the clear plan and the worksheet. Procurement likes the idea of a PO stub to reserve budget/slots; that will speed approvals on our side. A few quick clarifications from Legal/Procurement: 

- We typically need the MSA signed before we finalize the order form, but we're open to the PO stub + pilot approach if the DPA review is underway.
- Data residency: Cardinal requires EU residency for EU-scoped data; this account is US-only for now, so no additional clause needed.
- Can you confirm whether your SOC2 is a Type II for the last 12 months or a snapshot? We need the date range.

Procurement can aim to review the PO stub by Friday (06/27) if we get the SOC2 and SSO metadata by tomorrow.

Elena
Elena Morris
Senior IT Procurement
Cardinal Health AI

Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: evidence collection, SLA gating & signature timeline

Appreciate the quick reply. Short answers inline: 

- SOC2: Type II, report period 2024-07-01 to 2025-06-30 (we'll share the bridge letter and control matrix this afternoon).
- PO stub: we'll upload a signed stub (non-binding) to your drive and Cc procurement. Good to hear you can target Friday review.
- MSA vs Order form: Redwood prefers to have key commercial terms locked (order form) while MSA/DPA redlines are finalized — we'll accept the MSA signature occurring on the same week as order form signature so long as the DPA is materially agreed and no new security exceptions are added after pilot. 

To minimize legal friction, proposed concrete gating language for the MAP: 
- Pilot activation allowed upon receipt of SOC2 Type II and provisioning details.
- Procurement PO stub issued to reserve slot; order form signature contingent on no material DPA issues discovered during legal review.
- If a material security issue is found during the pilot, Redwood will pause customer data ingestion and work with Cardinal to remediate; acceptance will be deferred until remediations are validated.

I've uploaded: naomi_MAP_v1.xlsx and a copy of the SOC2 bridge letter (link in the MAP tab). Karthik — can you review the DPA redline and call out any must-have clauses (LI, IP carve-outs, data residency language)?

Naomi

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Morris <elena@cardinalhealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Jun 2025 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: evidence collection, SLA gating & signature timeline

Thanks Naomi — looping in a couple quick legal points so procurement has visibility. Quoting Naomi's proposed gating: "order form signature contingent on no material DPA issues discovered during legal review." Two notes: 

1) "Material DPA issues" needs definition for the MAP to avoid circular waits. Suggest we define that as: (a) any data security clause that would require code changes or a new hosting region; or (b) any indemnity/liability exposure beyond our negotiated cap. Minor wording tweaks (audit, breach notice timelines, subprocessor lists) should not block the order form.

2) For pilot SLAs, Legal can accept reduced uptime SLOs (e.g., 95% during pilot) but we need a clear remediation and rollback plan. Please add an explicit acceptance test: 7 consecutive business days within target latency and error-rate thresholds, OR achievement of three sample evaluation prompts with X% correctness (we should align on metrics with CS).

Finally, procurement may ask for a shortened signature window; we can allow a 10-business-day DPA review turnaround if Cardinal commits to specific sign-off owners (legal + security) and the PO stub is issued.

I'll attach suggested language in the redline and will aim to push the DPA via our DocuSign team once terms are agreed.

Laura Bennett
Corporate Counsel, Redwood Inference
